title: Implement no-drops safety check in backend
description: Implement backend safety validation to ensure no DROP or ALTER statements are executed that would modify or drop existing database objects.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend rejects DDL containing DROP statements
Backend rejects DDL containing ALTER statements that modify existing objects
Only CREATE statements for new objects are allowed
Descriptive error is returned for rejected DDL

REVIEW FINDING (blocks approval): security bypass in validateDdlSafety ALTER branch, empirically confirmed via containerized vitest - combined clauses are wrongly allowed: 'ALTER TABLE employee ADD COLUMN nickname TEXT, DROP COLUMN age;' and 'ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT c UNIQUE (a), DROP COLUMN b;' both return safe:true. Root cause: the additive allow-checks (ADD+COLUMN / ADD+CONSTRAINT) run before the destructive reject-checks (DROP COLUMN / DROP CONSTRAINT / MODIFY COLUMN / RENAME / ALTER COLUMN) and short-circuit with continue, so a destructive clause hidden after an additive clause is not rejected.

Impact: violates acceptance criteria #1 (Backend rejects DDL containing DROP statements) and #2 (Backend rejects DDL containing ALTER statements that modify existing objects). A P0 safety gate must not have a bypass.

Required fix: reorder the ALTER branch in backend/src/services/ddl-safety.ts so destructive/modifying checks (DROP COLUMN, DROP CONSTRAINT, MODIFY COLUMN, RENAME, ALTER COLUMN) are evaluated BEFORE the additive ALLOW checks (ADD CONSTRAINT / ADD COLUMN), OR reject any ALTER containing destructive keywords regardless of additive clauses. All single-clause cases and typecheck already pass.
Reviewer decision: changes-requested. Ticket returned to implementer (backend-developer) to fix the bypass and re-submit for review.
